result.title: Weakly Supervised Fish Segmentation through Point-Supervised Tracking and Motion-Informed Language
result.comment: Accepted to IEEE OCEANS 2026 Monterey, 7 pages
result.summary: Understanding the properties of fish populations is increasingly important. Analyzing fish length, width, and mass is integral to maintaining healthy stock in the aquaculture industry, while counting wild fish populations supports marine conservation and coastal reef restoration efforts. Deep learning-based segmentation models offer a promising means of obtaining such information at scale. Most of these models, however, require costly and time-consuming per-pixel segmentation labels for training, which can take up to two minutes per fish to annotate manually. To address this inefficiency, we propose a weakly supervised segmentation pipeline that requires only point-labeled data (one click per fish) to produce accurate segmentation masks. Our pipeline consists of four stages. First, a point-supervised tracker predicts point annotations for each frame. These points are then converted into motion-informed language expressions, which guide a language-conditioned segmentation model (LMPM++) to capture temporal consistency and produce candidate segmentation masks. Finally, optical flow and background subtraction are applied as post-processing filters to suppress noise from incorrect segmentations. Experiments on the DeepFish dataset show improvement in foreground mean intersection over union (mIoU) as compared to baseline models.

AI.brief_summary: 面向鱼类分割标注昂贵的问题，提出仅用点标注（每鱼一次点击）的弱监督流水线：点监督跟踪器逐帧外推点标注，将其转为含运动信息的语言表达以条件化分割模型 LMPM++，再用光流与背景差分做后处理过滤。
AI.relevance_reason: 把运动线索转写成语言表达来条件化分割、并以后处理过滤抑制错误掩码的做法，可能与 LVR 中「视觉证据筛选」及语言提示承载任务必要信息的思路相通，可供核查；但该文不涉及推理期状态生成或答案对 latent 内容的使用。
